dossiers.title: Dome Keeper
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Core play alternates between mining below the dome for resources and returning before alien waves strike; pressure to decide when to retreat makes resource trips strategically tense.
Players describe choosing between dome weapons, repairs, digging upgrades and transport gadgets, with upgrade order shaping later survival.
Procedural mining terrain, short runs and changing gadgets invite experiments, but some players find the set of meaningful choices relatively shallow.
The recurring dig-return-defend loop is satisfying to some, while others find the mining and research repetitive once the core system is understood.
Wave timers, gathering resources and escalating attackers demand time management, with adjustable challenge suited to differing play styles.
Russian and English players praise the distinctive pixel art, atmospheric music and cohesive audiovisual presentation.
A co-op discussion describes resource sharing and individual upgrades, making coordination under attack part of the group challenge.
Co-op players report that shared expenses and upgrade allocation can be unforgiving when partners have different skill levels.
The cyclical demands of mining, retreating, upgrading and defending create a concise rhythm of short-term decisions.
Players disagree on long-term depth: some enjoy the compact risk-and-reward system, while others want more lasting rewards and variety.

dossiers.title: Afterimage
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 11 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Players praise fast two-dimensional combat with several weapon classes and mobility abilities that enable different fighting approaches.
The huge connected world has varied biomes and abundant secrets, but its size sometimes leaves players feeling lost or stuck backtracking.
Normal combat and many bosses are relatively forgiving for some genre veterans, though challenge and enjoyment depend on build and selected difficulty.
Players debate stat-heavy upgrades and small numerical gains even while appreciating the breadth of equipment to discover.
Some player accounts cite long detours and poorly signposted requirements for alternative endings as frustrating interruptions to exploration.
Hand-drawn scenery, colors and music repeatedly receive praise across player communities.
Critics say the elaborate worldbuilding does not always make the main narrative or multiple endings clear and satisfying.
Some players enjoy the fast combat feel, while others find certain spells and attack animations interrupt movement or offer little value.
Long playtime and optional pathways provide plenty of exploration, but some see the repeated traversal as padding.
An English-language report finds narrative localization unclear, while a Russian player comments positively on the Russian presentation; this does not prove the current status of either translation.
Some action-focused players favor weapon skills over magic, describing spells as less practical with aerial moves and dodges.

dossiers.title: 你已经猜到结局了吗
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 11 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The central player task is a lateral-thinking mystery: ask yes/no questions, test hypotheses, then infer what actually occurred in each hidden story.
The base catalogue has many short cases; players praise Steam Workshop support for new community-written riddles and extra stories.
Fans praise the mysterious short plots, distinctive artwork and expressive hosts that frame each case.
Mysteries vary in quality and challenge; some players enjoy surprising deductions but others say answers are too obvious or depend on guessing.
Players complain about long answer transitions, repetitive confirmation prompts and several menu steps to switch cases or review story information.
Solving a fixed riddle reduces replay appeal, while workshop additions supply new content of variable quality.
Opinions on the connected plot diverge: some like the dialogue and mysteries, while others find the ending unfulfilling.
Older community players report problems interacting with an answer or unlocking a conclusion; whether these still occur after updates is not established.
A completion-focused account describes moving through primary and bonus mysteries to unlock further linked narrative scenes.
A positive player also warns that some community-created riddles may be shallow compared with the official cases.
A critic feels guided question choices can constrain experimentation rather than allow open lateral deduction.
